questions.q: What is an 'IAM hub' or broker in an enterprise identity landscape?
options: A type of SAML assertion
A backup copy of the user directory
A Salesforce-specific Connected App
A central identity system that downstream applications trust, instead of trusting each other directly
questions.explain: An IAM hub (Okta, Entra ID, Ping Identity, etc.) acts as the central trusted IdP that every downstream application relies on, rather than every application maintaining direct trust with every other application.

questions.q: Why does a hub-and-spoke trust model scale better than point-to-point trust as an organization adds applications?
options: Point-to-point trust grows combinatorially with the number of apps, while hub-and-spoke only needs one relationship per app to the hub
Hub-and-spoke eliminates the need for any authentication at all
Point-to-point trust is always faster to configure regardless of scale
It doesn't scale better; both require the same number of relationships
questions.explain: With point-to-point trust, the number of pairwise relationships grows much faster than the number of apps. A hub-and-spoke model needs only one relationship per app, to the central IdP.

questions.q: In most mature enterprise identity landscapes, what role should Salesforce usually play relative to a dedicated IAM hub?
options: Salesforce should replace the HR system as the authoritative identity source
Salesforce should always be the authoritative IdP for the whole enterprise
Salesforce should usually act as an SP relative to the hub, acting as an IdP only for a narrower set of apps that specifically launch from inside Salesforce
Salesforce should never be configured for SSO at all
questions.explain: A dedicated IAM hub is usually the better authoritative IdP for the whole landscape, with Salesforce acting as an SP for standard access, and as an IdP only for apps meant to be launched from inside Salesforce itself.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the standard discovery questions an architect should ask before designing a Salesforce identity integration?
options: How many Apex triggers does the org currently have?
What is the org's current API version?
What color scheme does the client prefer for reports?
What system is the authoritative identity source, and does it already have a Salesforce connector?
questions.explain: Identifying the authoritative identity source and its existing Salesforce connectivity is foundational discovery work, needed before any technical SSO configuration should begin.

questions.q: What is usually the most common root cause of identity projects that need significant rework later?
options: Skipping landscape/discovery work and jumping straight into technical SSO configuration
Using SAML instead of OIDC
Enabling My Domain too early in the project
Choosing the wrong OAuth scope on a connected app
questions.explain: The lesson emphasizes that the technical configuration (SAML settings, connected apps) is usually the easy part — skipping discovery of the broader identity landscape and trust boundaries is what causes costly rework.
